nodes.title: Reject input that is not a string
nodes.why: The contract allows strings only, so a TypeError beats a wrong length for null, a number or an array.
nodes.alternative: Coerce the input with String(s) and keep going.
nodes.tradeoff: Strict input checking surfaces caller bugs early; coercion would hide them.

nodes.title: Remember where each character last appeared
nodes.why: Knowing the last index of a character lets the window jump past a repeat in one step, instead of shrinking one character at a time.
nodes.alternative: Keep a Set of the window and remove characters from the left until the repeat leaves, as approach 2 does.
nodes.tradeoff: The Map keeps an entry for every distinct character seen; the Set keeps only the window but may remove several characters in one step.

nodes.title: Move the start forward only
nodes.why: An index from before the window is not a repeat inside it. In "abba" the final a would otherwise pull the start back to 0 and count a window with two b.
nodes.tradeoff: Both forms state the same rule; the comparison names the window boundary, the max hides it in arithmetic.

nodes.title: Measure the window at every step
nodes.why: Once the start has moved, the window from start to i holds no repeat, so its length is a candidate at every index.
nodes.alternative: Measure only when a repeat moves the start, then once more after the loop.
nodes.tradeoff: Measuring every step costs one comparison per character and leaves no end case to forget.

nodes.title: Reject input that is not a string
nodes.why: The contract allows strings only, so a TypeError beats a wrong length for null, a number or an array.
nodes.alternative: Coerce the input with String(s) and keep going.
nodes.tradeoff: Strict input checking surfaces caller bugs early; coercion would hide them.

nodes.title: Keep the window in a Set
nodes.why: The Set answers whether the next character is already in the window in constant time.
nodes.alternative: Search the window with indexOf or includes on the string.
nodes.tradeoff: A search scans the window at each step, which turns the pass quadratic on long input; the Set keeps it linear.

nodes.title: Shrink from the left until the repeat leaves
nodes.why: Removing characters from the left keeps the window contiguous and free of repeats.
nodes.alternative: Jump the start past the last index of the character, as approach 1 does.
nodes.tradeoff: Each character enters and leaves the Set at most once, so the pass stays O(n), though one step may remove several characters.

nodes.title: Measure after adding the new character
nodes.why: With the repeat gone and the new character added, the window from start to end is a valid candidate.
nodes.alternative: Track the Set size, which equals the window length.
nodes.tradeoff: inWindow.size reads the same number; the index form matches approach 1 and the prose.
